name: Dal Tadka
steps: Pick over the toor dal, then rinse several times until the water is less cloudy. Finely chop the tomato and coriander, keeping the coriander aside for finishing.
Put the drained dal, measured water and turmeric in a pressure cooker. Follow the manufacturer’s fill limit for pulses, which foam during cooking.

Pressure-cook according to the cooker instructions, about 12–18 minutes at pressure. Let pressure release safely before opening; the dal should crush easily with the back of a spoon. If still firm, cook further before continuing.
Whisk or mash the cooked dal lightly, leaving a little texture. In a separate pan, warm the ghee over medium heat and add cumin; let it sizzle until fragrant without turning black.

Add the chopped tomato and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until soft and pulpy. Reduce the heat, stir in chilli powder briefly, then immediately mix this tempering into the dal so the spice does not burn.
Add salt and simmer uncovered for about 5 minutes, stirring the base. Add hot water a little at a time until the dal pours easily from a ladle, then finish with coriander and serve hot.
tips: For a thinner dal add hot water gradually. Avoid burning the chilli powder.
substitutions: Any substitution changes the recipe: recheck allergies, Jain rules and quantities.
notes: Prices are sample ingredient-cost assumptions. Replace with supplier rates before procurement.
